title: System, Method, and Delay-Tolerant Radio Wire Framing for Sovereign Off-Grid Financial Settlement over LoRa Mesh Networks, Sub-GHz Radio Transceivers, and Disconnected Edge Gateways
description:
A formal technical disclosure and defensive publication establishing prior art for an off-grid, delay-tolerant financial settlement protocol and compact radio wire framing architecture (X402-LORA) operating across uncoordinated Sub-GHz Long Range (LoRa) mesh radio networks (868 MHz / 915 MHz ISM bands).

By compressing the entire atomic financial state transition—comprising an immutable transaction UUID, ADR-062 256-lane sequential watermark nonce, cross-currency corridor identifier, 64-bit base-unit value, absolute expiration epoch, 256-bit sender public key, 64-bit recipient account identifier, and an Ed25519 cryptographic signature—into an exact 144-byte binary wire payload, the settlement voucher fits entirely within the single-packet Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) of Semtech SX1261/SX1262/SX1276 transceivers and Meshtastic broadcast frames without packet fragmentation.

Establishes offline double-spend mitigation via localized 256-lane nonce partitioning (allocating dedicated offline sub-lanes 0..31), sub-10ms signature verification on low-power microcontrollers (ESP32-S3 / ARM Cortex-M4), and opportunistic store-and-forward batch ingestion into Layer-1 DAG consensus upon encountering edge gateways. Published pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) and EPC Article 54(2) establishing defensive prior art.
